subtype: Winking in professional or cross-cultural settings [Regulating]
passage: Kamal had been at the marketing firm for two weeks when a new colleague, Rukmini, took the lead on a difficult presentation and nailed it. Across the boardroom, Kamal's first instinct was to give her a quick wink and a thumbs-up, the sort of thing he did with his college friends. Then he stopped. He remembered the mixed reactions to a wink from his old manager, and that Rukmini was from a different country and he barely knew her. A wink might look flirtatious, or rude. Instead he waited until the meeting ended, walked over and said, "That last slide was really clear. Nice work." Rukmini smiled. "Thank you. That means a lot."

qa.a: He had been at the marketing firm for two weeks.

qa.q: Why did Kamal decide against winking at Rukmini?
qa.a: He worried that in a work setting with someone new from another country, a wink could be read as flirtatious or rude, so he chose clear words.

qa.q: What did Kamal do instead of winking?
qa.a: He waited until the meeting ended and told Rukmini in words that the last slide was really clear.

qa.q: How might Rukmini have felt if Kamal had winked?
qa.a: She might have been confused or uncomfortable, not knowing his meaning, whereas the words let her feel simply appreciated.

grounding: A young adult avoids winking at work because it can be misread, and chooses clear words to respect others.

"Before you fly out on Monday," Sunaina said, folding Nandini's shirts into the suitcase, "one small thing. At home you wink at people when you agree with them. It's cute. It's also how you and I joke."
"Okay?"
"Not everywhere. In some places a wink at work or from a stranger can read as flirty or rude. Your manager won't know it's just your style."
Nandini laughed. "So no winking at Mr Novak."
"Say it in words. 'Good point, I agree.' Nobody misunderstands that."
"What if I forget?"
"Then explain quickly and smile. People forgive when they can tell you meant well." Nandini put her hand on her heart. "Words first. Got it, didi."

passage:
In my first week as an intern at a design studio in Bengaluru, I winked at my manager, Nitin.
He'd asked if I could finish the poster by five. I said, "Done," and winked. It's what I do with my friends; it means "I've got this."
His face changed. Just for a second. He looked away, cleared his throat and said, "Okay. Thanks." Then he was a bit stiff with me all afternoon.
I replayed it all evening. Did he think I was flirting? Being cheeky with my boss?
Next morning I said, "Nitin, yesterday I winked. That's just a habit from college, it meant 'I'll handle it.' Sorry if it came across oddly."
He relaxed. "Thanks for saying. It did confuse me for a second."
Now at work I use words. "I'll handle it by five." It's less fun, but nobody has to guess.
- Hafsa

qa.q: By what time did Nitin want the poster finished?
qa.a: By five.

qa.q: What was Hafsa feeling while replaying the wink that evening?
qa.a: Hafsa felt anxious and embarrassed, worried the wink had seemed flirtatious or cheeky to a boss.

qa.q: What did Hafsa change at work, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Hafsa now uses clear words instead of winking, because a wink can be misread at work and words leave nothing to guess.

qa.q: How did Nitin read the wink?
qa.a: The wink confused Nitin for a moment, and he seemed unsure whether it was flirtatious or disrespectful.

grounding: The account shows a young adult's habitual wink being misread at work and choosing clear words instead.

Supervisor's note - Kishore, hotel front office, Friday
Our new trainee, Santosh, is warm and quick with guests. One habit needs attention. When he hands over room keys, he often winks and says, "All sorted." With our regular guests from the city, it gets a laugh.
Today an elderly guest travelling from abroad looked startled when he winked at her. She stepped back slightly, then asked me, quietly, whether the young man was "being fresh." I reassured her.
After the shift I spoke to Santosh. He was embarrassed. "Sir, I only meant everything's done."
I told him I believe him. But a wink can read as flirting, or as not taking someone seriously, depending on the person and where they come from. At work, with new people, words are safer: "Your room is ready. Is there anything else I can help with?"
He agreed straight away. By evening he'd dropped the wink completely.

qa.q: What does Santosh say when he hands over room keys?
qa.a: "All sorted."

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling when Kishore raised the wink?
qa.a: Santosh felt embarrassed, since he had meant only that everything was done.

qa.q: What advice did Kishore give, and why?
qa.a: To use clear words instead of winking with new guests, because a wink can be misread as flirting or disrespect in some cultures.

qa.q: How did the elderly guest read Santosh's wink?
qa.a: She was startled and wondered whether he was being inappropriate, not seeing it as a friendly signal.

grounding: The supervisor's note shows a trainee's wink being misread across cultures and choosing clear words at work instead.

Monday
First month at the new job and I've already done something awkward. After the team meeting, Bhupen from accounts made a joke about the printer, and I winked at him. Like I'd wink at my college friends: "Ha, good one."
He went red and looked at his shoes. At lunch he sat at a different table.
Oh no. Did he think I was flirting? In my old friend group a wink is nothing. But he doesn't know me, and I don't know where he grew up or what a wink means there.
I found him at the water cooler. "Bhupen, sorry, the wink earlier. That was just me laughing at your printer joke. Didn't mean anything else."
He laughed, relieved. "Okay. I wasn't sure. In my family, winking is... a thing."
Rule for work: save the winks for college friends. Use words.
- Charu

qa.q: Where did Charu find Bhupen?
qa.a: At the water cooler.

qa.q: What was Bhupen feeling when Charu winked at him?
qa.a: Bhupen seemed embarrassed and uncomfortable, going red and sitting elsewhere, unsure if the wink was flirtatious.

qa.q: Which choice of Charu's worked, and why?
qa.a: Explaining the wink plainly at the water cooler worked, because it cleared up the misunderstanding with clear words.

qa.q: How did Bhupen's family background shape how he read the wink?
qa.a: In Bhupen's family winking carries more meaning, so he took it more seriously than Charu's friends would.

grounding: The diary shows a young adult's wink being misread by a new colleague and deciding to use clear words at work.
